clue.text: Took possession of a suitable number

parts.note: something suitable is fitting or proper for the occasion
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a number

explanation.surface: Someone has claimed a fitting quantity of something for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a suitable number' reads as one phrase, but it splits: the suitable word, then a Roman numeral as the number.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize or take something for one's own use is the verb's sense, here in the past tense.

clue.text: The story of Bill Noble

parts.note: AC, short for ..., is a bill
a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: The tale of a nobleman called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill Noble' reads as a man's name; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative report of events, as in an eyewitness's version of what happened.

clue.text: Redhead embraced by French marshal just wants to belong

indicators.note: the head of red is held inside the marshal's name, as if hugged

parts.note: Petain was a Marshal of France in the First World War
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: A red-haired person in the arms of a French marshal only wants to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just wants to' is padding linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate or be relevant to something, as a matter that belongs to a subject.

clue.text: Perilous position of the eye-witness

explanation.surface: The witness who saw it all is now in a tight corner.
explanation.walkthrough: Being put 'on the spot' is being pressed awkwardly; a witness was literally there at the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being put in a difficult situation, and also literally present at the scene, like a witness.

clue.text: It's a bit sticky when the siren goes haywire

indicators.note: something that goes haywire goes wildly out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Things get awkward when the alarm starts malfunctioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes haywire' rearranges SIREN.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum exuded by pine trees is a tacky, adhesive substance.

clue.text: Measure a top engineer over a long time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pieces sit over, that is above, the long time

parts.note: CRE, Commander Royal Engineers, is the senior engineer officer in a British Army formation
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Gauge a senior engineer's service over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: CRE (Commander, Royal Engineers) is a British Army post.
explanation.definitionFit: Land area reckoned in acres is a measure of extent.

clue.text: Beg to escape from centre attacks

indicators.note: the letters slip out of the middle of these words, a run escaping from them

explanation.surface: Someone pleads to get away from attacks in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead or implore earnestly is the same as to beg.

clue.text: Old Botswana

parts.note: the former name of the southern African country before independence in 1966

explanation.definitionFit: The British protectorate's name for the territory that became the independent republic in 1966.

clue.text: It's taken out except when right inside

indicators.note: the word for right is placed inside the other word, the clue saying so directly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is removed in every case except where the right is kept within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' looks like part of the sentence's grammar but is itself the word cut open.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage extracted from a longer book or film is a thing taken out of it.

clue.text: Time that's done appears elastic

explanation.surface: A completed spell of time seems to have been pulled longer.
explanation.walkthrough: A prison term served is a 'stretch'; 'stretch' fabric is elastic. 'appears' only links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell in prison is slang for the time a convict serves, and stretchy fabric gives elastically.

clue.text: Give them to your sons tomorrow if your daughters don't like them

definitions.text: Give them to your sons tomorrow if your daughters don't like them

parts.words: Give them to your sons tomorrow if your daughters don't like them
parts.note: a reworking of the nursery rhyme line about giving the buns to your sons if your daughters don't like them

explanation.surface: A parent's advice on passing unwanted food from daughters to sons.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'If your daughters do not like them, give them to your sons'; 'tomorrow' places the clue on Good Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiced buns marked with a cross, eaten on Good Friday and celebrated in the nursery rhyme.

clue.text: This contractor has a lot of pull

definitions.text: This contractor has a lot of pull

parts.words: This contractor has a lot of pull
parts.note: pull reads as influence, but it is literal pulling of loads by lorry

explanation.surface: A builder or supplier with plenty of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: A firm that moves goods by road is a 'haulage contractor', and hauling is pulling; 'pull' pretends to mean clout.
explanation.definitionFit: The business of carrying goods by road names the trade of a road-freight contractor, whose work is literally pulling loads.

clue.text: Most close the net around the god of war

indicators.note: the net is wrapped around the god, so its letters enclose his name

parts.note: taken as the word net
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: A fighter closes the net around Ares himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of close, meaning least distant, is the same as most close.

clue.text: Not an unusual name

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so the preceding letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone insists a certain name is perfectly common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges NOTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's first name, as in the actor Anton Walbrook.

clue.text: Churchman helps to stop recent orgies

indicators.note: the words help to make it, each supplying part of a run of letters across them

explanation.surface: A clergyman assists in halting the latest wild parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric who leads the singing of a choir or congregation in a cathedral is a church official.

clue.text: Difficult session? Not here !

parts.note: session read as a sitting: a comfortable seat is no place for a hard sitting

explanation.surface: A tough meeting is promised not to take place here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'session' is a sitting down; the seat offers the opposite of difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep upholstered armchair is a seat where any sitting is comfortable.

clue.text: Prepared as the conjurer is with this

definitions.text: Prepared as the conjurer is with this

parts.words: Prepared as the conjurer is with this
parts.note: a magician comes ready with equipment for his tricks, the gear itself being the thing named

explanation.surface: A magician is ready for the show with his kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The conjurer is prepared because he has his gear: the definition is the equipment itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment or gear for a task, such as the props and devices a stage magician uses.

clue.text: Self — satisfied pea — shelling Dickensian?

parts.note: a smug character from Our Mutual Friend whose name splits as a pea pod and a snap

explanation.surface: A smug Dickens figure busy shelling peas.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Podsnap in Our Mutual Friend is the type of complacent self-satisfaction; his name suggests snapping open pea pods.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's smug, complacent character in Our Mutual Friend gave English the word podsnappery.

clue.text: Its root makes a tasty dish

indicators.note: the letters of the first words make the dish, being rearranged to form it

explanation.surface: The root vegetable turns into a delicious meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges ITSROOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: A king writing about a princess

indicators.note: the writing goes about, that is around, the princess

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
Princess Ida is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta

explanation.surface: A monarch is penning something about a royal daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary king of Phrygia whose touch turned everything to gold.

clue.text: Plague spirit rising over falling water

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A plague of drink comes up while water pours down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns RUM into MUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An infectious disease of cattle, and an old word for a pestilence.

clue.text: Many a company has its gangsters !

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: Lots of firms employ hoodlums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives the Roman numeral D for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed robbers who worked in gangs in India and Burma.

clue.text: A learned cleric has one son, Joseph

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a learned clergyman's degree
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scholarly churchman has a single boy, called Joseph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joseph' looks like the son's name in the story; it is the definition, the essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was the English essayist who co-founded The Spectator, so his first name defines him.

clue.text: Limit of sartorial excellence for squares

explanation.surface: The best dressed are a bunch of squares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed to the nines' is the height of smartness; nine is three squared.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for dressing to perfection, and the numbers that are squares of three.

clue.text: Pipe grain to the horse

parts.note: corn is grain such as wheat or maize
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: Someone pipes feed to the horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' looks like a verb about delivering grain; it is the noun, a tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe whose bowl is made from a dried maize cob.

clue.text: He took the devil by the nose

definitions.text: He took the devil by the nose

parts.words: He took the devil by the nose
parts.note: the legend of a saint who seized Satan by the nose with red-hot tongs

explanation.surface: Someone bravely grabbed Satan by the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says the saint, a smith, gripped the devil's nose with tongs from his forge.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth-century Archbishop of Canterbury of legend who pinched Satan's nose with tongs.

clue.text: Fabulous nights!

parts.note: fabulous here means of fables: the nights of the famous story collection with Scheherazade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means full of fables, not wonderful: the Thousand and One Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in the title of the tale collection told by Scheherazade, describing its desert origin.

clue.text: Matriarchal bonds

parts.note: the ties of a mother's domestic garment, standing for maternal control

explanation.walkthrough: A son 'tied to his mother's' these is dominated by her.
explanation.definitionFit: The ties of a kitchen pinafore, idiomatically the hold a mother keeps on a grown child.
